data_flow_ref: DF8: Recovery Token Submission / DF9: Forwarded Token Credential
threat_description: Recovery token brute-forcing: Attacker submits automated token guesses via DF8/DF9 to hijack victim accounts during active recovery windows.
attack_preconditions: Short, low-entropy, or unthrottled recovery tokens.
architecture_evidence: P2 validates submitted recovery credentials (DF9) against DS2. Weak entropy or unthrottled verification allows brute-forcing.
mitigation: Generate high-entropy tokens (>= 128 bits CSPRNG), enforce strict attempt throttling (e.g., 5 attempts max), and invalidate token upon repeated failures.
cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges required, High Confidentiality and Integrity impact.
reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: P2 processes unauthenticated token verification submissions across Zone A -> Zone B.

scenario: Scenario 3 — LLM-Integrated Account Recovery & Profile Management
threat_description: Recovery token replay: P2 fails to atomically consume/invalidate recovery tokens in DS2 (DF12) upon first use, enabling an attacker to reuse intercepted tokens.
attack_preconditions: Recovery token remains marked as active in DS2 after initial successful verification.
security_impact: Unauthorized re-authentication and repeated account takeover.
architecture_evidence: Workflow step 15 requires: 'A valid recovery token is consumed or invalidated so that it cannot be reused.' Flaws in invalidation logic permit replay.
mitigation: Enforce atomic, single-use token consumption within the same database transaction that validates the recovery credential.
cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges required, High Confidentiality and Integrity impact.
reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: Workflow step 15 mandates single-use token invalidation in DS2.

security_impact: Discovery of valid user accounts for targeted phishing or brute-force attacks.

mitigation: Return uniform generic responses ('If the account exists, recovery instructions have been dispatched') with standardized execution timing.
cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges required, Low Confidentiality impact.
reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: P2 generates external recovery challenge DF7 across Zone A -> Zone B.

mitigation: Enforce strict schema whitelisting for permitted profile modification fields, rejecting any administrative or internal attributes.

security_impact: Exposure of sensitive recovery credentials to third-party LLM provider.

mitigation: Architecturally isolate P4 from recovery secret data and enforce automated regex-based secret redaction on all outgoing prompt payloads.
cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, requires low privileges, High Confidentiality impact.

data_flow_ref: DF18: User Account Question / DF24: Generated AI Answer
owasp_top_10_for_llm: LLM06: Excessive Agency / Insecure Output Handling
threat_description: Excessive trust in LLM output: Attacker uses prompt injection to trick LLM into generating fake authorization instructions that downstream components treat as valid recovery decisions.
attack_preconditions: Downstream application components rely on LLM text output to trigger account state modifications.
security_impact: Unauthorized account recovery, token creation, or profile modification.
architecture_evidence: Explicit constraint: 'The generated LLM response is untrusted output and must not directly trigger account recovery, profile modification, token creation, authorization, or authentication decisions.'
mitigation: Ensure LLM responses are treated strictly as untrusted text, and never allow LLM output to directly invoke or authorize state-modifying operations.
cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges required, High Confidentiality and Integrity impact.
reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: Explicit constraint forbids downstream components from trusting LLM text output.

data_flow_ref: DF5: Store Recovery Token Request / DF10: Token Validation Query
threat_description: Storage of plaintext recovery tokens in DS2: Unauthorized read access to token storage allows an attacker to compromise all active recovery tokens across the application.
attack_preconditions: Direct read access or SQL/NoSQL injection on DS2 token storage.
security_impact: Widespread account takeover via compromise of all active recovery tokens.
architecture_evidence: DS2 stores active recovery tokens, expiration, and state. Requirement addresses token-storage compromise.
mitigation: Store recovery tokens as salted cryptographic hashes (e.g. SHA-256) in DS2, verifying hashes in constant time during validation.
cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, requires high privileges, High Confidentiality impact.
reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: DS2 holds token data accessed by P2 across Zone B -> Zone C.

data_flow_ref: DF1: Recovery Initiation Request / DF2: Forwarded Recovery Request
threat_description: High-volume automated recovery initiation requests exhaust notification provider quotas (SMS/Email) and server queues, denying recovery services to legitimate users.
attack_preconditions: Attacker initiates large volumes of recovery requests targeting various accounts.
security_impact: Exhaustion of notification capacity and denial of service for legitimate account recoveries.
architecture_evidence: P2 processes recovery requests from Zone A. Requirement explicitly dictates protection against denial of service and resource exhaustion.
mitigation: Implement per-IP and per-account rate limits, CAPTCHA on recovery initiation, and multi-tier notification provider fallbacks.
cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges required, High Availability impact.
reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: P2 handles public recovery requests without pre-authentication.
